subject: SDKGrove onboarding and rate limits / endpoint migration plan
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@tapco.com>

Subject: SDKGrove onboarding / rate limits questions

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for the demo last week. Two quick priorities from our side as we kick off implementation: 1) getting the SDKGrove client installed and running on our staging cluster, and 2) clarifying expected rate limits + migration steps for moving from our current endpoint to Redwood's hosted endpoints.

We attached a short infra overview (tapco-infra-overview.pdf). Our staging cluster will run Node 18 containers behind an API gateway; engineers are worried about 429 spikes during batch jobs. Can you share a recommended client configuration (timeouts, retries, batching settings) and a suggested cutover cadence?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we want to start the sandbox integration next week.

Thanks,
Samantha
Engineering Manager, TapCo

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@tapco.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SDKGrove onboarding / rate limits questions

Hi Samantha — thanks for the infra doc, that helps. Below is a concise onboarding plan + operations guidance we recommend for first-pass integration. Attaching our SDKGrove onboarding checklist and a short mutual action plan as well.

TL;DR (what to do this week)
- Install SDKGrove Node client (npm install @redwood/sdkgrove).
- Configure environment: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_ENV=staging, REDWOOD_REGION=us-west1.
- Use streaming responses for long-generation jobs to avoid large payloads.

Sample configs (Node):
- SDK init (Node):
const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdkgrove');
const client = new Redwood({apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: 'us-west1', timeoutMs: 15000});

- Retry policy (recommended):
  * idempotent requests: up to 3 retries, exponential backoff 200ms -> 800ms -> 1600ms with full jitter
  * non-idempotent (generate/chat): perform single retry on network error, otherwise prefer fallback model variant to avoid duplicate side effects

- HTTP timeouts: connectTimeout=2000ms, readTimeout=12000ms (adjust upward for long generations).

cURL quickstart (staging):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"sdkgrove-2b","input":"summarize: ...","stream":false}'

Endpoint migration and cutover guidance
1) Sandbox (day 0–3): point a single staging service to hosted staging endpoint (region us-west1). Monitor 429s and p99 latency.
2) Ramp (day 4–7): route 10% -> 50% -> 100% of non-critical traffic through Redwood with canary headers. Implement request tagging (X-Client-Env: tapco-staging) to filter metrics.
3) Production cutover: use traffic shaping at gateway (5-minute windows), enable prefix caching for repeated prompts, and increase concurrency gradually. Keep fallback model variant in routing policy for sudden capacity drops.

Rate limit matrix (hosted tiers / observed):
- Default sandbox: 60 reqs/min per API key, burst up to 120 for 1 minute
- Production baseline: 600 reqs/min per project, burst to 1,200 with token-based throttling
- Large reserved/dedicated: negotiated; recommend starting with reserved 10k reqs/min if TapCo expects heavy batch processing

Retries and backoff summary (short):
- 429s: treat as rate-limit — backoff with exponential jitter, reduce client concurrency by 25% after second 429 in 30s window.
- 5xx: retry with exponential backoff up to 3 times.
- Network errors/timeouts: immediate retry once, then escalate to fallback path.

Attachments included: sdkgrove-onboarding-checklist.xlsx, mutual-action-plan-TapCo.docx

Action items for TapCo engineers:
- Install SDK and run the quickstart within staging today.
- Run a 30-minute load test (100 concurrent clients) and share p95/p99 latency + 429 counts.
- Confirm a 1-hour window on Friday for canary traffic shift to 10%.

Internal notes (cc'd): Monica — please advise on recommended default model variant and any quantization presets for sdkgrove-2b we should call out. Vivek/Vanessa — can you confirm if dedicated capacity should be proposed in the follow-up quote?

Cheers,
Soojin 
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: sdkgrove-onboarding-checklist.xlsx, mutual-action-plan-TapCo.docx

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 13:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SDKGrove onboarding / rate limits questions

Quick internal follow-up (internal only):

For TapCo staging: recommend starting with sdkgrove-2b-fp16 (default quantization profile) to keep memory bounded and latency predictable. If they see token-level variance, we can switch to sdkgrove-2b-int8 for cost savings but warn on slight quality delta.

Caching / KV guidance:
- Enable prefix/KV caching on repeated prompt families with TTL=300s. For batch summarization workloads, use ephemeral session keys and cache hits to reduce per-token cost.

Ramp schedule suggestion for ops team:
- Day 1: smoke, single worker to hosted staging (monitor).
- Day 2: 10% canary for non-critical endpoints, throttled to 30 rps per instance.
- Day 4: 50% if p99 < 800ms and 429s < 0.1% of traffic.

Vanessa — please prepare an updated pricing recommendation for reserved capacity if they plan >50k reqs/day. Aditya — can you validate that our default timeout config (connect=2s, read=12s) appears in the SDK quickstart?

—Monica

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@tapco.com>

I'll sign the mutual action plan and upload it to the link in the MP doc (coming shortly). Thanks again for the clear plan — schedule confirmed.

Best,
Samantha
